tier1.text: Mitochondria make ATP, the cell's main energy-carrying molecule. They do this by cellular respiration, which uses oxygen and the energy stored in nutrients. Their inner membrane has many folds, called cristae, which add surface area for making ATP. Muscles use huge amounts of ATP, so muscle cells are packed full of mitochondria.

sentences.text: Mitochondria make ATP, the cell's main energy-carrying molecule.

quotes.quote: Scientists often call mitochondria (singular = mitochondrion) “powerhouses” or “energy factories” of both plant and animal cells because they are responsible for making adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the cell’s main energy-carrying molecule.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: They do this by cellular respiration, which uses oxygen and the energy stored in nutrients.

quotes.quote: Cellular respiration is the process of making ATP using the chemical energy in glucose and other nutrients. In mitochondria, this process uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide as a waste product.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Their inner membrane has many folds, called cristae, which add surface area for making ATP.

quotes.quote: In the mitochondria, the inner membrane is extensively folded, which increases surface area for ATP production.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The inner membrane is highly folded into winding structures with a great deal of surface area, called cristae.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Muscles use huge amounts of ATP, so muscle cells are packed full of mitochondria.

quotes.quote: One of the organ systems in the body that uses huge amounts of ATP is the muscular system because ATP is required to sustain muscle contraction. As a result, muscle cells are packed full of mitochondria.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
